subject: reasoning
question:
G, H, I, J, K, L and M are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table(but not necessarily in the same order).

J sits third to the left of G. M sits second to the left of K. Only G sits between H and M. L is not an immediate neighbour of J. How many people sit between I and M when counted from the right of I?
solution:
Given: 

G, H, I, J, K, L and M are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table(but not necessarily in the same order).

J sits third to the left of G.
